newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends weaker as soybeans collapse.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends weaker as soybeans collapse.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on Thursday as weakness from the soybean pit overwhelmed bullish input from USDA's weekly export data, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended January 23 totaled 1.285 million tonnes, above expectations for 800,000 to 1.0 million tonnes.
But traders said soybeans continued to be the floor leader and weakness in that key market outweighed bullish corn news.
Soybean exports were on the low end of expectations and beneficial rains fell in dry pockets of southern Brazil, easing concerns of drought-related losses.
News China sold 100,000 tonnes corn to the Philippines also weighed on prices and suggested world buyers were looking elsewhere for supplies, traders said.

Options were again active. Cargill Investor Services bought 700 July $2.80 calls at 9-1/4 to 9-1/2, Prudential Securities bought 500 March $2.70 puts at 3/4 cents per bushel and sold $2.80 calls and puts, traders said.
Cargill Investor Services also bought 500 March $2.80 calls and sold 500 March $2.90 calls.
Corn closed three to 1-1/4 cents per bushel lower with March down 1-1/4 at $2.73-3/4.
